blocks.text: If there is one thing that audiences try to find in a narrative, it is the ability to relate to it in whatever way that may be. As creatives say, “Representation matters,” and the DreamWorks Animation’s “Forgotten Island” attests to this notion. Inspired by Filipino culture and mythology, the animated film is set in the 1990s Philippines as it follows two childhood friends, Jo (H.E.R) and Raissa (Liza Soberano), who become trapped in the mystical world of Nakali. From the get-go, the film is very conscious of bringing Filipino culture to the screen, not only through its larger cultural elements but […]...
